messages:
elaine (Sales): Hey team — POC with Concordia is failing when they attach long docs + embeddings in one request. Getting a 413 / "payload too large" from our gateway. Repro steps below, can we triage?

Tom S (Solutions): Ack, dropping in. Do we have snippet of the request? body size?

elaine (Sales): They sent ~3.2MB JSON (base64 attachment + 40k tokens). curl they used: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d @big_payload.json
```
Response: 413 Request Entity Too Large + nginx upstream sent no response.

Rishabh (Eng): Thanks — sounds like gateway limit (nginx client_max_body_size) or a proxy choking on huge single requests. Also check request latency/timeouts for large streaming. Any logs?

elaine (Sales): Katie pulled the gateway logs, attached snippet: 
```
2026-03-20T14:02:11Z FAIL client_max_body_size exceeded while reading client request
2026-03-20T14:02:11Z upstream prematurely closed connection
```

Katie (Support): Confirmed. This is the hosted gateway rejecting >2MB by default. We have a couple of paths: 1) advise customer to chunk client-side and stitch results, 2) switch to upload-to-storage + reference (presigned S3 URL) then server-side fetch, 3) for Dedicated we can raise gateway limits. Which do they prefer?

elaine (Sales): They asked for a quick workaround for POC — minimal code change on client side preferred. They want to avoid S3 flow right now.

Tom S (Solutions): Recommend on-the-fly chunking: split the long document into N overlapping windows, call embeddings/generation per chunk, then aggregate. Suggest overlap ~= 100-200 tokens to keep context. For streaming generation, use chunked streaming and stitch with a simple merge heuristic. I'll paste a small pseudo flow.

Tom S (Solutions): ```
# pseudo
chunks = sliding_window(doc, window=4096, overlap=200)
responses = [api.generate(prompt=chunk) for chunk in chunks]
final = stitch(responses)
```
This avoids >2MB and keeps POC moving.

Rishabh (Eng): Two implementation notes: 1) For embeddings + generation in same flow, do embeddings calls per chunk and store vector ids, then use server-side rerank on consolidated vectors. 2) If they absolutely need single-call semantics, we can provide a temporary increase for POC via a support ticket (but not ideal at scale).

elaine (Sales): Client engineer asked whether gzip helps — could we accept gzipped JSON?

Katie (Support): Gateway already unzips if Content-Encoding: gzip is set, but some proxies drop gzipped payloads. We can accept gzip but still have limits on decompressed size. So gzipping might help borderline cases, but not 40k tokens.

Rishabh (Eng): Also watch out for model max_context_tokens: even if gateway lets it through, model runtime will truncate at its token limit. For POC, recommend a server-side pre-check that rejects with helpful error: "document exceeds recommended max context; try chunking or use Dedicated".

elaine (Sales): Can we give them a quick code snippet + recommendation and ask if they want a temporary gateway bump for the demo?

Tom S (Solutions): I'll draft a one-pager: 1) short chunking example, 2) overlap suggestion, 3) embeddings+stitch approach, 4) contact for temporary lift (if demo on staging).

Katie (Support): I'll open a support ticket for a temporary gateway limit increase (internal only) in case they need it tomorrow — labeling it POC-critical.

deploy-bot: Note: support ticket #S-9421 created by Katie at 2026-03-20T14:08:22Z

elaine (Sales): Awesome — sharing Tom's snippet + our recommended approach now. Will update thread if they want the temporary bump. :thumbsup:

Tom S (Solutions): Quick add — if they can store raw text externally, we can also provide a presigned-url ingestion example to make the end-to-end flow more realistic for enterprise.

elaine (Sales): Perfect. Thanks all!
